label: thm-distributive-laws-for-union-and-intersection
tail:
VERDICT: CLEAN
BOUNDARY:
- Finite distributive laws with a = ∅, b = ∅, c = ∅: the logical equivalences in 1.3/1.4 hold because membership conditions reduce to false/false or true/true appropriately; equality follows.
- Finite distributive laws with arbitrary disjoint singletons: tested mentally, the membership equivalences are exact.
- Family laws with F = {∅}: then ⋃F = ∅, ⋂F = ∅; LHS a∩∅ = ∅, RHS ⋃{a∩∅} = ⋃{∅} = ∅; LHS a∪∅ = a, RHS ⋂{a∪∅} = ⋂{a} = a (since {a} nonempty). Holds.
- Family laws with F = {a}: ⋃F = a, ⋂F = a; LHS a∩a = a, RHS ⋃{a∩a} = ⋃{a} = a; LHS a∪a = a, RHS ⋂{a∪a} = ⋂{a} = a. Holds.
- Family laws with F = {a,b} where a∩b = ∅: ⋃F = a∪b, ⋂F = ∅; LHS c∩(a∪b) = (c∩a)∪(c∩b) by finite law, RHS ⋃{c∩a, c∩b} = (c∩a)∪(c∩b); LHS c∪∅ = c, RHS ⋂{c∪a, c∪b} = (c∪a)∩(c∪b) = c∪(a∩b) = c. Holds.
- F empty not considered for family forms; the theorem correctly restricts to F ≠ ∅.
- The family {a∪b : b∈F} is nonempty when F≠∅ (step 1.2), so L4 applies legitimately.
- Step 2.2’s case distinction (z∈a vs z∉a) is valid classically and does not depend on any extra hypotheses.
CHECKED: Read every numbered step (1.1, 1.2, 1.3, 1.4, 2.1, 2.2, 3.1) and every cited fact (L1–L8) against the supplied full texts of all dependencies; each citation is faithful and the proof steps are mathematically licensed by the cited facts.
